sourceNote: The Tripo P2 polar bear mesh with its quads (assets/models/polar-bear/README.md). The hand rig assets/models/polar-bear/tripo-hand/polar-bear.blend starts from it in headless Blender with the calls of tools/blender/body_armature.py (design 4.4, "Hand rig").
name: Polar bear
jointsNote: The places are the places of the source, mapped by the point edits of the hand rig (assets/models/polar-bear/README.md). The source places are in the body units and axes of the source pose: 1 unit from the soles to the top of the head, the soles at y = 0, +z forward, +x the left side. The right side mirrors the left side. The FBX has no armature, so each joint comes from sections of the mesh and its edge loops. Arm (axis y 0.67, z -0.01 to 0.02, height 0.21 at the root to 0.134 at x 0.31): the shoulder joint at x 0.125 inside the arm root (the armpit at x 0.16), the elbow at x 0.245 (0.52 of the arm from the shoulder to the wrist, as on the main polar bear), the wrist at x 0.355 where the paw widens, the knuckles at x 0.425 where the claws start, the tip at x 0.463. Leg: the hip joint at y 0.29, the knee at y 0.165 above the narrow shin, the ankle at y 0.062 above the heel, the ball of the foot at z 0.075, and the toe tips at z 0.14. Trunk: the joints on the middle line of the trunk sections. Head: the chin at y 0.79 and the top of the skull at y 1.0. Tail: the short tail at the back of the haunch at y 0.355. The palm faces down: the paws of the source lie flat with the claws at their front edge.
palmNote: The paws of the source lie flat with the claws curled down, so the palm faces down.

bind.note: legTurns gives the world turn of each left leg bone from the seated bind to the source: the thigh slopes 22 degrees down and 12 degrees out, and the shin leans 5 degrees forward of vertical, so that most of the thigh lies on the seat (uv run --no-project --with numpy python -I tools/rig/leg_turns.py <config> 22 12 5). The bind arms are those of the main polar bear. The bind paw of each arm turns about its bind forearm toward supination by bindSupination degrees (paw_supination() of tools/blender/rig_mesh.py).

colors.note: Each face takes the mean sRGB color of the color map at a grid of samples (add_surface()). The eye box holds the eyeballs (middles at x 0.034, y 0.924, z 0.095), and the nose box the black nose tip.

tone.note: No move. The hand route does not read the tone. The color map of the source replaces the face colors in the app.

colors.eyeBoxNote: The eye box holds the two loose eyeballs of the source (|x| 0.02 to 0.055, y 0.89 to 0.928, z 0.111 to 0.133, mapped by the point edits). The nose box holds the dark nose tip.

eyeShell.note: The values of the other meshes. The hand rig adds no eye fans (eye_fans=False).

chair.note: The piano bench of the pianist, as on the earlier Tripo polar bear (benchFitOf() of tools/body-module.ts).

armSegments.note: Each upper arm and each forearm has 4 deform segments, and each elbow and wrist a helper bone of this length in units.

rollSplitNote: The simple route splits the roll segments by place (roll_split() of tools/blender/simple_rig.py). The hand rig sets the same split in the exact rows of each arm ring (assets/models/polar-bear/README.md, "tripo-hand/polar-bear.blend").
chairNote: The seat of the rig in units of this body, as the property seat of the armature of tripo-hand/polar-bear.blend holds it.
bodyNote: The facts of the body (BODY_FACTS of tools/body-module.ts) beside the height: the crease angle 55, because the limb rings of the source have 15 or 17 vertices, and the Tripo mesh has many poles.
metersPerUnitNote: The scale of the app: H of the main polar bear (0.422795 m). The polar bear is the largest player.
eyeSizeNote: The head height H of the body in units, as body-module measures it on the export, before the head size. The hand rig keeps the eyes of the mesh, so it places no pea eye.
